structured_output.summary: This is a small, clean change. It adds `cancelFulfillment()` and its locators to the existing `OrderPage`, plus one spec. The spec uses the `ORDERS_SCENARIO`'s fulfilled order and asserts that the status reads "Unfulfilled" and the fulfil button is enabled, both right after cancelling and after a reload, so the reload proves the cancellation was saved. It type-checks cleanly and follows the suite's conventions. No checklist item fails.

items.evidence: spec lines 78-81 reload the page and assert status 'Unfulfilled' and fulfillButton enabled; that only passes if the cancel mutation persisted.
Every criterion is asserted: 'Unfulfilled' status (line 74), fulfil action offered again (line 75), still 'Unfulfilled' after reload (lines 79-80).

The new action is added to the existing OrderPage and reuses dialog/statusInfo/fulfillButton/timelineView, findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO. The `option` field copies the per-page pattern DraftOrderPage and AddressDialog already use, rather than borrowing AddressDialog's for a different dialog.
No fixed waits; the action waits on the dialog becoming hidden.
test comes from fixtures/test.ts, the test is not tagged parallel(), and nothing writes to the cache or seed.
Every locator is a data-test-id or a role; submit is scoped to this.dialog; option.first() is acceptable because the ticket says any warehouse is fine, matching DraftOrderPage's use.
Uses the scenario's existing fulfilled order via findOrderId; no set-up in the spec.
The order is looked up by its e2e key; no hard-coded ids or populatedb values.
Uses the fixture's default admin session; no UI sign-in.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0; the spec is in e2e/tests/orders/.
All locators and the multi-step action live on OrderPage.
New members are readonly fields initialised from this.page/this.dialog, in the existing class with constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
Has '// Arrange' and '// Act & Assert' comments, the suite's form.
One test covering one story, with a test.step per stage.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e.
Header comment at lines 55-59 explains what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first expect(locator).
Uses the ORDERS_SCENARIO constant; status strings are UI labels, as elsewhere in the suite.
No cleanup and no unique names.
No custom timeouts, retries or networkidle.
Relative imports keep .ts; test/expect come only from the fixture.
No any, casts or untyped gql.
The JSDoc on cancelFulfillment explains why (timeline view needed, warehouse choice); there are no narrating comments.
